page.overview:
Who is Henry Stephenson Blaine?

Dr. Henry Stephenson Blaine is a fictional character created by Lin Carter for his Xothic Legend Cycle.

Henry Stephenson Blaine, Ph.D., was the curator of the Manuscripts Collection at the Sanbourne Institute of Pacific Antiquities in Santiago, California (: "The Dweller in the Tomb"). He once studied Semitic Languages under George Gammell Angell (: "Out of the Ages").

In 1928, Dr. Blaine was in charge of making an inventory of the collection of artifacts and manuscripts that formerly belonged to the late Prof. Harold Hadley Copeland. Among Copeland's possessions was a carved jade idol of Zoth-Ommog and a copy of the Yuggya Chants. The idol gave Blaine nightmares and affected his mind, showing him images of the submerged Zoth-Ommog and trying to influence Blaine to remove the Elder Sign that kept the god imprisoned. At night, Blaine was afflicted with episodes of somnambulism in which he would walk to the beach at Wexton Pier with a paper containing an incantation copied from the Yuggya Chants. One night, he was found sleepwalking into the sea. Upon being awakened by the cops who located him, Blaine caught sight of at least one Yugg diving into the water. After that episode, Blaine was committed to Mercy Hospital Psychiatric Emergency under the care of Dr. Robinson Dambler. For the next two months, Blaine spoke nothing other than repeating the word "Yugg" and tried to blind himself 11 times. (: "Out of the Ages")

He was succeeded as curator by his friend and former assistant Arthur Wilcox Hodgkins. (: "Out of the Ages", "The Horror in the Gallery")
